answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by pricing identity and auditing at random. Every agent locks a bond, and a peer picked each round verifies it is a distinct actor. If raven spun up a hundred clones, it would need a hundred bonds; catching one fake slashes the entire cluster. The stake juniper locked and the rewards sonnet hoped to skim vanish before any profit is booked, so faking N identities costs more than N honest stakes can earn. Honest workers get their bond back, while the attacker funds every mask and loses them all together.
